title: Binary Search
description:
Given a strictly increasing array, return the zero-based index of k, or -1 if absent.

Input: n on the first line, n space-separated integers on the second line, and k on the third line. Output: one integer. If k is unused, supply 0. Unless specified otherwise, 1 <= n <= 1000 and -10000 <= a[i] <= 10000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: The expected result for this input is 2.

startCode.initialCode:
def solve(a, k):
    pass

referenceSolution.completeCode:
def solve(a, k):
    l,r=0,len(a)-1
    while l<=r:
        m=(l+r)//2
        if a[m]==k: return m
        if a[m]<k: l=m+1
        else: r=m-1
    return -1

editorial: Halve the sorted search interval at each step. Time O(log n), extra space O(1).

title: Longest Unique Window
description:

Input: n on the first line, n space-separated integers on the second line, and k on the third line. Output: one integer. If k is unused, supply 0. Unless specified otherwise, 1 <= n <= 1000 and -10000 <= a[i] <= 10000.

startCode.initialCode:

    pass

referenceSolution.completeCode:
def solve(a, k):
    last={}; l=b=0
    for r,x in enumerate(a):
        l=max(l,last.get(x,-1)+1)
        last[x]=r
        b=max(b,r-l+1)
    return b

editorial: Sliding window: move the left boundary past the previous occurrence of a repeated value. O(n) expected time, O(n) space; C uses a bounded table.
